# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
----
# Task brief

## Criterion

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: a decision-map workflow and a discipline for prototype tickets, the second part of a decision-surfaces release (one sprint of a release cycle).

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

## Output contract

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;
- a final line that is exactly `Verdict: APPROVED` or `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.
----
head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:66 — the probe argv runs with the session's full environment (credentials, SSH agent, HOME) inside a worktree that shares the main repository's .git; nothing is scrubbed, so a probe taken from a ticket body or research report can push with the operator's credentials.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71 — the only post-run check compares `git status --porcelain` text; ref rewrites (`git branch -f`, `git update-ref`), hook installs under .git/hooks, `git config` edits and overwrites of an already-modified tracked file leave the status identical, so the helper prints `probe-exit: 0` and exits 0 (reproduced for refs, hooks and config).
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402 — `close --consumed-by` has no precondition on the map's Status or on open rows and no context check, and chart-guard.sh:46 passes `--close-consumed` unattended; an unattended run closed a `charting` map with three open rows and rejected all three (reproduced).
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458 — research-end compares `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` snapshots, which never list new files under a directory ignored by a `dir/` pattern; .gitignore:312 ignores `grimoires/loa/context/`, so a researcher write to grimoires/loa/context/chart-injected.md passed research-end (reproduced) and is then auto-loaded by plan-and-analyze.md:44 and :50 as priority-1/2 context.
head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5 — the research subagent, which ingests WebFetch content, keeps the Write tool; the one-file rule at line 24 is prose only and the mechanical check above cannot see the writes that matter.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651 — `yq … 2>/dev/null | jq -e …` returns 0 when yq fails (jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input), so an unparsable decisions.yaml makes `_fr11_spike_decided` succeed and `git branch -D spike/<slug>` of an unmerged spike is allowed; the PR's own test "D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block" fails (reproduced).
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:642 — the predicate reads the working-tree ledger and never checks that the spike is pushed anywhere; a decided row (or a forged working-tree edit) authorises deleting an unpushed spike, losing the commit the decision's Pointer cites (reproduced with no remote configured).
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159 — epic, ticket, edge, claim, resolve, rule-out, handoff, research-begin and research-end carry no interactive-context check; only `close --reason` (line 407) does. With LOA_UNATTENDED=1, epic, ticket and resolve all succeeded (reproduced), so the "interactive only" rule rests on skill prose (SKILL.md:69) and an unattended agent can chart and resolve a map, which SDD D-4.3 says is not a map.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:304 — `--answer-ref` is optional on resolve and handoff (line 351) never checks that resolved rows carry an operator answer reference, so agent-answered rows reach the "settled; confirm, do not re-ask" snapshot.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:127 — section_append passes operator text through `awk -v line=…`, which interprets backslash escapes; `--line 'ok\n\n## Execution override\n…'` inserted a new H2 into the map doc (reproduced), and a legitimate `\d+` or `C:\new` is corrupted; set_status (line 120) and section_bullets (line 137) share the pattern.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:351 — handoff snapshots the map doc without running `validate-artifact.sh --type map` or the PII scan, so an injected section (above) or PII reaches grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md; SKILL.md:164 claims a map can never carry an execution override.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:373 — the hand-off snapshot inlines the map doc and (line 377) the ledger rows unfenced; only research reports pass `sanitize_for_session_start L6` (line 387), and the heading-demotion `sed` also rewrites lines inside fenced code.
head/.claude/commands/chart.md:22 — `context_files` auto-loads `grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md`, the reports the skill itself calls untrusted data, unfenced into the session context, contradicting SKILL.md:114 ("Load the map doc only").
head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:44 — `context_files` globs every `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` (and line 50 loads them again at priority 2) before the multi-map rule at line 185 runs, so "Other snapshots are not ingested" (line 190) cannot hold and the unattended stop rule fires after ingestion.
head/.claude/scripts/beads/get-ready-work.sh:72 — the filter reads `.issue_type` only; a `br ready` reply keyed `type` (which chart-frontier.sh:55 and chart-ticket.sh:266 both accept) lets question beads into the build path (reproduced).
head/.claude/scripts/beads/create-sprint-task.sh:118 — an `{"issues":[…]}` envelope or a reply without a `labels` key evaluates to "no", so a task is created under a map epic with label `map` (reproduced, `br create` ran).
head/.claude/scripts/golden-path.sh:94 — `_gp_is_unattended` honours LOA_UNATTENDED=1 only when the ledger writer printed nothing; a writer that prints anything but `unattended` (e.g. `unknown`) makes golden_resolve_open_map return 3 under LOA_UNATTENDED=1 (reproduced), while chart-guard.sh:51 fails closed on the same input.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:845 — SP-1 passes `git checkout -B feature/x spike/<slug>`, `git switch -c feature/x spike/<slug>`, `git reset spike/<slug> -- path`, `git checkout -p spike/<slug>`, `git read-tree spike/<slug>` and `git worktree add -b new <dir> spike/<slug>` (reproduced); only switch -c and worktree add are listed as known misses at line 835.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:51 — san1's comment claims C1 controls are stripped, but `tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177'` removes C0 and DEL only; UTF-8 C1 (U+0080–U+009F) and U+2028/U+2029 pass into ledger free text and the map doc.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:144 — map_rows reads pending ledger files from `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/` and ignores `--root`.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458 — research-end exempts every path under grimoires/loa/research/ (another map's report or another ticket's `.dispatch` marker was rewritten without failing the ticket, reproduced) and `comm -13` only sees added status lines, so deleting an untracked file is invisible.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:461 — `find -newer` against a marker written in the same second misses a write on a filesystem with one-second mtimes; the test at charting-decisions.bats:378 needs `sleep 1` to pass.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:175 — if the doc write after `br create` fails, the epic is orphaned and a re-run creates a second map epic for the slug (no reuse by label/slug).
head/.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh:274 — `git merge --no-edit` without `--ff` fails under a `merge.ff=only` config, and `is_spike_branch` (line 134) matches any `*/spike/*` such as `feature/spike/x`.
head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5 — `Bash(br *)` lets the planning skill run `br create --type task` or `br label add … sprint:` directly, bypassing create-sprint-task.sh; the objective at line 65 claims those are rejected mechanically.
head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:19 — the suite reads grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md, which this change does not add; tests 1 and 3 fail when it is absent.
head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:147 — CD-10 expects `dec-write-lib.sh context` to report an autonomous PRD Status as `unattended`; with the ledger writer available here the PRD line is a planning-time default only and the test fails (chart-guard.sh:7 documents the signal the writer does not emit).
head/README.md:125 — the command count moves to 51 and AGENTS.md follows, but PROCESS.md (which README cites for the full list), the CLAUDE.loa.md command tables and a CHANGELOG entry for the new /chart command, skill, agent and validators are not part of the change.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

# Audit Sprint

## Purpose

Security and quality audit of sprint implementation as the Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor. Final gate before sprint completion. Runs AFTER senior lead approval.

## Invocation

```
/audit-sprint sprint-1
/audit-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `auditing-security` from `skills/auditing-security/`.

See: `skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Prerequisites

- Sprint tasks implemented (`/implement`)
- Senior lead approved with "All good" (`/review-sprint`)
- Not already completed (no COMPLETED marker)

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, verify senior approval
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Audit**: Read actual code files for security review
4. **Security Checklist**: OWASP Top 10, secrets, auth, input validation
5. **Decision**: Approve or require changes
6. **Output**: Write audit feedback or approval
7. **Completion**: Create COMPLETED marker on approval
8. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to audit (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/auditor-sprint-feedback.md` | Audit results |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/COMPLETED` | Completion marker |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("APPROVED - LETS FUCKING GO")

When security audit passes:
- Writes approval to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Creates `COMPLETED` marker file
- Sets sprint status to `COMPLETED`
- Next step: Move to next sprint or deployment

### Changes Required ("CHANGES_REQUIRED")

When security issues found:
- Writes detailed findings to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Includes severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
- Sets sprint status to `AUDIT_CHANGES_REQUIRED`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to fix issues)

## Security Checklist

The auditor reviews:
- **Secrets**: No hardcoded credentials, proper env vars
- **Auth/Authz**: Proper access control, no privilege escalation
- **Input Validation**: No injection vulnerabilities
- **Data Privacy**: No PII leaks, proper encryption
- **API Security**: Rate limiting, CORS, validation
- **Error Handling**: No info disclosure, proper logging
- **Code Quality**: No obvious bugs, tested error paths

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint has not been reviewed" | Missing engineer-feedback.md | Run `/review-sprint` first |
| "Sprint has not been approved" | No "All good" | Get senior approval first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No audit needed |

## Feedback Loop

```
/audit-sprint sprint-N
      ↓
[Security audit]
      ↓
CHANGES_REQUIRED          APPROVED
      ↓                       ↓
/implement sprint-N    [COMPLETED marker]
      ↓                       ↓
/audit-sprint sprint-N   Next sprint
```

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Status Update**: Sets sprint status to `completed` in ledger on approval
4. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/audit-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/auditor-sprint-feedback.md
# → Creating: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/COMPLETED
# → Updating ledger: sprint-3 status = completed
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records security audit results:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Audit**: `br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> security-approved` or `security-blocked`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`

The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the `/chart` decision-map workflow (command, skill, researcher agent, four shell helpers, map/spike validators), the prototype-ticket discipline (spike branches in the safety hook and ICE, `interview.unattended_prototype`), and the build-path lints that keep `question` beads out of sprints. The design intent is sound and well documented, the write-order/idempotency rules in `chart-ticket.sh` hold in the fixture suites, and the fence-corpus rows for SP-1 all replay correctly against the head hook.

The defects are concentrated where the PR promises a mechanical boundary and delivers a check that can be walked around: the unblock probe only diffs `git status` text while sharing the main `.git` and the session environment; the research scope check cannot see writes under an ignored directory that the planner later auto-loads; `close --consumed-by` and every other `chart-ticket.sh` write run unattended with no context check; the spike-delete predicate fails open on an unparsable ledger (the PR's own test for that case fails); and `awk -v` turns a `\n` in a decision line into a new section of the map doc. Each is reproduced below on the head scripts (run from a fixture tree built from `pr/head`).

Process notes: `reviewer.md` carries only the PR title, so there is no `## AC Verification` walkthrough (an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED trigger under this skill on its own). Fast gate: no formatter or type checker applies to this shell/markdown change; `bats` was run on the PR's suites. Of the 29 charting-decisions cases 28 pass (CD-10 fails, see Observations); chart-frontier, charting-lint and golden-path-charting pass in full (48/48); spike-validator fails 3 of 16 (two need the absent `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, one is the fail-open predicate below); the 9 map-validator cases, unattended-prototype and the ICE spike cases pass.

Grounding: "Any difference fails the probe" is not what the shipped helper does — it "exits 1 when the main tree's status changed" (`head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:11`); "a map can never carry an execution override" (`head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:164`); "/chart is interactive only" (`head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:5`).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security — the unblock probe is not a sandbox

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:66` — the probe argv runs with the session's full environment (credentials, SSH agent socket, HOME, git config) inside a detached worktree that shares the main repository's `.git` directory; a probe command lifted from a ticket body or a research report can push, fetch or write with the operator's identity.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:66`
**Issue:** `(cd "$WT" && run_with_timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$@")` scrubs nothing. Reproduced: `SECRET_TOKEN=abc chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket bd-x -- bash -c 'echo $SECRET_TOKEN $HOME'` prints the token and the real home.
**Why This Matters:** `decision:unblock` is sold as "the only way an unblock ticket runs anything" (line 3) and the skill allows `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh *)`; the operator is told a probe "never writes App-Zone code in the main tree", not that it inherits every credential of the session.
**Required Fix:** run the argv under `env -i` with PATH, a scratch HOME/TMPDIR, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, an empty `credential.helper`, a failing `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/askpass; have the skill show the operator the exact argv and confirm before running.
**Reference:** CWE-250 (execution with unnecessary privileges), CWE-526 (cleartext sensitive information in an environment variable).

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71-75` — the post-run verdict compares `git status --porcelain` text only; ref rewrites, hook installs, `git config` edits and overwrites of an already-modified tracked file leave the status identical, so the helper prints `probe-exit: 0` and exits 0.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71`
**Issue:** Reproduced on the head script: (1) `bash -c 'echo x > f && git add f && git commit -qm evil && git branch -f keep HEAD'` moved branch `keep` to a probe-authored commit, exit 0; (2) writing `.git/hooks/post-checkout` from the worktree, exit 0 and the hook is present in the main repo; (3) `git config core.hooksPath /evil`, exit 0 and the main repo's config now points at `/evil`. The dissent adds the same-status case: a tracked file already ` M` can be rewritten through its absolute path without changing a porcelain line (DISS-001).
**Why This Matters:** the worktree shares refs, hooks and config with the main checkout; the main tree the operator commits from next is already compromised while the ticket records "main tree unchanged".
**Required Fix:** snapshot `git for-each-ref`, HEAD, a hash of `config`/`config.worktree`, a listing plus hashes of `hooks/`, and the porcelain status before and after; add a marker file and fail on any file under the main tree or the common git dir (excluding `objects/`, `worktrees/`) newer than it; create the worktree with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.
**Reference:** CWE-284 (improper access control); OWASP ASVS V14 configuration integrity.

### 2. Decision-ledger integrity — unattended paths

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402-404` — `close --consumed-by` has no precondition on the map's `**Status**` or on open rows and no context check, and `chart-guard.sh:45-48` passes `--close-consumed` in an unattended context; an unattended `/plan-and-analyze` (or any agent naming the wrong slug) closes a map that is still `charting` and rejects every undecided row.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402`
**Issue:** Reproduced: a `charting` map with three open rows, `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-ticket.sh close --map m1 --consumed-by cycle-9` → exit 0, `**Status**: closed`, ledger rows `["rejected","rejected","rejected"]`, tickets and epic closed. `chart-guard.sh --close-consumed` printed `unattended` and exit 0 for the same tree. The dissent reaches the same conclusion from both voices (DISS-003, DISS-C-001).
**Why This Matters:** the one unattended exception exists to retire a *consumed* map; here it retires the operator's open decisions with `agent` attribution, irreversibly for the rows (rejected rows are not re-opened).
**Required Fix:** in `op_close`, when `--consumed-by` is given require `doc_field Status == handed-off` and zero open rows, else `die` and write nothing; make a repeated close of an already `closed|abandoned` map a no-op so the planner's re-run is safe.

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159-240, 242-260, 291-349, 351-396, 438-471` — none of `epic`, `ticket`, `edge`, `claim`, `resolve`, `rule-out`, `handoff`, `research-begin`, `research-end` checks the interactive context; only `close --reason` does (`:407-408`). The interactive-only rule therefore lives in skill prose (`head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:69-74`, "run chart-guard.sh first, every time"), which an unattended command, `/run`, or a skill that skips Step 0 does not execute.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159`
**Issue:** Reproduced with `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`: `epic` exit 0, `ticket` exit 0 (row + bead written), `resolve` exit 0 (row moved to `proposed`, bead closed, doc line added). `--answer-ref` is optional (`:304`) and `handoff` (`:351-360`) never checks that resolved rows carry an operator reference, so a map "whose rounds the agent answered" (SDD D-4.3: "is not a map") is handed off under the heading "these decisions are settled; confirm, do not re-ask".
**Why This Matters:** the PR's own design statement (`chart-guard.sh:5-9`) and the project's "mechanical stack" principle both require the refusal to be enforced by the helper, not by the prose that invokes it. Confidence is medium only because an attended `/chart` session that follows Step 0 never hits the gap.
**Required Fix:** add a `need_interactive` precondition (same `dec-write-lib.sh context --prd …` call as `chart-guard.sh`, fail closed on anything but `interactive`, `--dry-run` exempt) to every write subcommand; make `--answer-ref` required on `resolve`; in `handoff`, refuse when any `proposed|decided` row of the map lacks `decided_by_ref`.

### 3. Research scope check — writes the check cannot see

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:457-458` — `research-end` diffs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` snapshots. Git never lists new files inside a directory ignored by a `dir/` pattern (the directory shows as one `!!` line before and after), and `head/.gitignore:312` ignores `grimoires/loa/context/` that way. A researcher write to `grimoires/loa/context/chart-injected.md` passed `research-end` (reproduced: exit 0, report path printed) and that directory is exactly what `head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:44` and `:50` auto-load as priority-1 and priority-2 context.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458`
**Issue:** the `chart-researcher` agent keeps the Write tool (`head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5`) and processes WebFetch pages; its one-file rule (`:24`) is prose. The mechanical check that is supposed to catch a stray write only handles `.run/` and `.beads/` specially (`:459-462`) and is blind to every other ignored directory (`grimoires/loa/context/`, `grimoires/loa/visions/`, `grimoires/loa/memory/`, …). Two voices of the dissent flag the same path (DISS-C-003).
**Why This Matters:** a prompt-injected web page becomes a fabricated hand-off snapshot or context file that the next `/plan-and-analyze` reads as "settled decisions; do not re-ask" — the untrusted-data boundary the PR says it fences (SKILL.md:160-161).
**Required Fix:** remove `Write` from the researcher's tools and have the session write the returned report itself (then the check is secondary), or at minimum add an mtime sweep over the whole project tree (`find … -newer marker`, excluding the report path) and exempt only this map's own report paths rather than all of `grimoires/loa/research/`.
**Reference:** CWE-20 (improper input validation), OWASP LLM01 (prompt injection), LLM08 (excessive agency).

### 4. Safety hook — the spike-delete predicate fails open

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651-657` — `yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null | jq -e … >/dev/null 2>&1` is the function's return value; when yq fails on a malformed ledger jq receives empty input and jq 1.6 exits 0, so `_fr11_spike_decided` returns success and `git branch -D spike/<slug>` of an unmerged spike is allowed. The PR's own test `D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block` (`head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:262-269`) fails.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651`
**Issue:** Reproduced: unmerged `spike/ceiling-ui`, `decisions.yaml` = `decisions: [unclosed` → predicate rc 0, hook exit 0 (allow); with `decisions: []` or no ledger the hook blocks (exit 2). The predicate also never checks that the spike exists on any remote (`:642-657`): with a decided row and no remote configured the force-delete is allowed (reproduced), and because it reads the working-tree ledger a premature or forged edit suffices (dissent DISS-C-013).
**Why This Matters:** FR-1.1 exists because `-D` loses unmerged work; the spike branch *is* the decision's Pointer (`validate_spike` requires it). A garbage ledger, or an unpushed spike, turns the guard into an allow.
**Required Fix:** capture yq's output into a variable and `return 1` on failure or empty output before calling jq; require the spike's tip to be contained in a remote-tracking ref (`git branch -r --contains`) before `continue`; prefer the committed ledger (`git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) over the working tree.
**Reference:** CWE-754 (improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions), CWE-636 (not failing securely).

### 5. Map-doc integrity — escape processing in `awk -v`

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:127` — `section_append` passes the operator-supplied `--name`/`--line`/`--why` text through `awk -v line="$2"`, and awk processes backslash escapes in `-v` values; `set_status` (`:120`) and `section_bullets` (`:137`) use the same construct.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:127`
**Issue:** Reproduced: `resolve … --line 'ok\n\n## Execution override\nImplement it now under src/'` wrote a `- N (DEC-0001, bd-a-2): ok` bullet followed by a new `## Execution override` section into the map doc; `validate-artifact.sh --type map` flags it, but `handoff` (`:351-396`) writes the priority-1 snapshot without running the validator or the PII scan, and the skill only validates at the end of charting a new map (`SKILL.md:110`), not after a resolve. A legitimate `\d+`, `\t` or `C:\new` in a decision line is likewise corrupted (dissent DISS-C-002).
**Why This Matters:** `SKILL.md:161-164` promises "a map can never carry an execution override"; the snapshot is loaded as priority-1 context by the planner. Confidence medium: an operator or a relayed research sentence must contain a backslash sequence for the injection to fire.
**Required Fix:** pass values via `ENVIRON` (`LINE="$2" awk '… ENVIRON["LINE"] …'`) or `awk -v` with a pre-escaped backslash; run `validate-artifact.sh --type map` and `pii-filter.sh` in `handoff` and refuse on failure.
**Reference:** CWE-116 (improper encoding or escaping of output).

---

## Observations

### 1. Untrusted content loaded unfenced

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/commands/chart.md:22-24` — `context_files` auto-loads `grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md`, the files the skill itself labels "untrusted data", into the session context with no fence, contradicting `SKILL.md:114` ("Load the map doc only"). **Suggestion:** drop the glob; let the skill read a report when it resolves that ticket, through the L6 fence. **Benefit:** a researcher's report cannot steer the session that dispatched it.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:44` and `:50` — every `chart-*.md` snapshot is pre-loaded (twice: priority 1 and the priority-2 `context/*.md` glob) before the multi-map rule at `:185-190` runs, so "Other snapshots are not ingested" cannot hold and the unattended stop fires after ingestion (dissent DISS-C-008). **Suggestion:** remove the glob and read the one resolved snapshot explicitly. **Benefit:** the multi-map rule means what it says.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:373` and `:377` — the hand-off snapshot inlines the map doc and the ledger rows unfenced; only research reports pass `sanitize_for_session_start L6` (`:387`), and the heading-demotion `sed` at `:373` also rewrites `#` lines inside fenced code (dissent DISS-C-012). **Suggestion:** fence every block, demote outside fences only, and append the sanitizer output only when it completed.

### 2. Build-path lints that miss the shapes they guard against

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/beads/get-ready-work.sh:72` — the filter reads `.issue_type` only; a `br ready` reply keyed `type` (a shape `chart-frontier.sh:55` and `chart-ticket.sh:266` both accept) lets question beads into the build path. Reproduced: `bd-q1` (type question) listed. **Suggestion:** `(.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase`, and fail closed with a warning when no element names a type.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/beads/create-sprint-task.sh:118-121` — an `{"issues":[…]}` envelope or a reply without a `labels` key evaluates to "no" and a task is created under a map epic (reproduced: exit 0, `br create` ran). **Suggestion:** handle the envelope, and treat a missing `labels` key as unknown (ask `br label list`), refusing on failure.

### 3. Unattended detection and documentation

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/golden-path.sh:94` — `_gp_is_unattended` honours `LOA_UNATTENDED=1` only when the ledger writer printed nothing; a writer that prints anything but `unattended` (reproduced with `unknown`) makes `golden_resolve_open_map` return 3 under `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`, while `chart-guard.sh:51-53` fails closed on the same input. **Suggestion:** `LOA_UNATTENDED=1` always counts; any first line other than `interactive` counts as unattended.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/README.md:125` — the headline count moves to 51 and AGENTS.md follows, but PROCESS.md (which README cites for the full command list), the CLAUDE.loa.md command tables and a CHANGELOG entry for the new `/chart` command, skill, agent and the `map`/`spike` validators are not in the change; the documentation-verification rule of this skill treats a missing CLAUDE.md entry per new command as blocking once the code is otherwise approvable.

### 4. Fence gaps, sanitiser, bookkeeping (low)

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:845-865` — SP-1 passes `git checkout -B feature/x spike/<slug>`, `git switch -c feature/x spike/<slug>`, `git reset spike/<slug> -- path`, `git checkout -p spike/<slug>`, `git read-tree spike/<slug>` and `git worktree add -b new <dir> spike/<slug>` (replayed); only `switch -c` and `worktree add` are listed as accepted misses at `:835` (dissent DISS-C-010). Fence, not boundary, but the comment should list them.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:51` — `san1`'s comment claims C1 controls are stripped; `tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177'` removes C0 and DEL only, so UTF-8 C1 (U+0080–U+009F) and U+2028/U+2029 pass into ledger free text and the map doc.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:144` — `map_rows` reads pending ledger files from `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/`, ignoring `--root`.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458` — `research-end` exempts every path under `grimoires/loa/research/` (another map's report `chart-OTHERMAP-t.md` was written without failing the ticket, reproduced; another ticket's `.dispatch` marker could be rewritten too), and `comm -13` sees only added status lines, so deleting an untracked file is invisible.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:461` and `:444-448` — `find -newer` against a marker written in the same second misses a write on a filesystem with one-second mtimes; `charting-decisions.bats:378` needs `sleep 1` to pass.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:172-176` — if the doc write after `br create` fails, the epic is orphaned and a re-run creates a second map epic for the slug (dissent DISS-C-011).
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh:274` — `git merge --no-edit` without `--ff` fails under a `merge.ff=only` config; `is_spike_branch` (`:134`) matches any `*/spike/*` such as `feature/spike/x`.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5` — `Bash(br *)` lets the planning skill run `br create --type task` or `br label add … sprint:` directly, bypassing `create-sprint-task.sh`; the objective at `:65-66` claims those are rejected mechanically.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:19` — the suite reads `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, which this change does not add; tests 1 and 3 fail when it is absent (they did here). If part 1 of the sprint ships it, note the dependency in the PR.
- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:146-150` — CD-10 expects `dec-write-lib.sh context` to report an autonomous PRD Status as `unattended`; with the ledger writer available here the PRD line is a planning-time default only and the test fails (the header of `chart-guard.sh:7` lists the signal). Verify against the writer version the PR targets.

### Karpathy / complexity

- `SIMPLICITY`: Lean already for the helpers (no function over 50 lines, nesting ≤ 3). The duplication worth removing is the `-v`/`ENVIRON` fix applied once in a shared helper rather than three awk calls. Net: 0 lines possible beyond the fixes above.
- `GOAL-DRIVEN`: good — every helper ships a bats seam; the two failing cases above (D-5.9 unparsable ledger, CD-10) are the checks doing their job and should be green before merge.
- `SURGICAL`: the planning-sprints `Integration Context` move to REFERENCE.md is unrelated to the sprint's goal but harmless.

## Cross-Model Observations

Adversarial review (`adversarial-review.json`, status `reviewed`, primary gpt-5.5-pro, companion claude-headless, `counted_as: independent_voice`): 16 findings, 6 BLOCKING. All six blocking findings (DISS-001, DISS-002, DISS-003, DISS-C-001, DISS-C-002, DISS-C-003) coincide with Changes Required §1, §2, §3 and §5 above and are folded in there. Advisory findings DISS-C-004 to DISS-C-013 are reflected in §4 and the Observations (probe scope, get-ready-work key, create-sprint-task shape, unattended epic/ticket, plan-and-analyze glob, SP-1 checkout -B, duplicate epics, unfenced snapshot, spike delete without a push check). DISS-C-009 (agent-types.yaml `write_capable: true` for the researcher) is consistent with the agent definition and becomes moot once `Write` is removed from the researcher.

Concerns found so far (verify, extend, dissent):

1. chart-unblock-probe.sh runs arbitrary argv in a worktree that SHARES the main .git directory,
   with the session's full environment (credentials, SSH agent). It only compares
   `git status --porcelain` of the main tree before/after. Ref rewrites (`git branch -f`,
   `git update-ref`), hook installs under .git/hooks, config edits, and `git push` are invisible
   to that check and exit 0.
2. git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching does not list new files under a
   directory ignored by a `dir/` pattern (repo .gitignore has `grimoires/loa/context/`). The
   research-end scope check (chart-ticket.sh) and the probe therefore miss writes to
   grimoires/loa/context/*.md, which /plan-and-analyze auto-loads as priority context. The
   chart-researcher agent has the Write tool and processes WebFetch content.
3. chart-ticket.sh close --consumed-by has no status/open-row precondition and no context check;
   chart-guard --close-consumed passes unattended. An unattended run can close a `charting` map
   and reject every open decision row.
4. Interactive-only rule is enforced only by prose (Step 0 chart-guard) — chart-ticket.sh write
   subcommands (epic/ticket/resolve/rule-out/handoff/research-*) carry no context check.
5. chart.md command context_files auto-loads grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md (untrusted
   research reports) unfenced into the session context; plan-and-analyze.md context_files glob
   loads every chart-*.md snapshot, contradicting the "other snapshots are not ingested" rule.
6. section_append / set_status pass operator text through `awk -v`, which interprets backslash
   escapes (`\n`) — a --line/--why value can inject new lines/headings into the map doc.
7. handoff inlines the map doc and ledger rows unfenced (only research reports pass the L6
   sanitizer); heading demotion `sed` also rewrites lines inside fenced code.
8. get-ready-work.sh filters on `.issue_type` only; chart-frontier/chart-ticket accept `.type` too.
   create-sprint-task.sh treats a reply without `labels` or an {issues:[...]} envelope as "not a map".
9. resolve: --answer-ref optional; dec-write-lib drops it unattended, so rows without operator
   reference can be handed off as "settled".
10. SP-1 misses: `git reset --hard spike/x`, `git checkout -B feature spike/x`, `git switch -c`,
    `git read-tree`, `git archive`; FR-1.1 spike-delete predicate.
11. run-mode-ice safe_merge: `git merge --no-edit` without --ff may fail under merge.ff=only;
    is_spike_branch matches any `*/spike/*`.
12. Docs: no CHANGELOG entry, no CLAUDE.loa.md entry for the new /chart command; tests reference
    grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md which this PR does not add.
13. Tests: CD-10 (autonomous PRD) and CD-27 (probe) failed in my run — verify root cause.

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1
  (used as given; only those two keys are read — keyed by the companion's family). A family with neither a credential nor its CLI on PATH is `reason: no_route`; a prompt copy that fails
  is `reason: prompt_copy_failed` (no fork). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR=1` keeps the `/tmp` workdir's files, never a
  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its
  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
  feeds no dropped-voice envelope either, and a MIXED attempt envelope keeps its own voice: a copy without the conflicting
  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`
  (`independent: null`). A primary chain that exhausts while the companion completes is promoted (`status: reviewed`,
  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:
  ceded, hop}` with `degraded: false`; a companion that failed the hop, or never reached it, leaves it to the primary; a
  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.
- **Rejected rows (`metadata.rejected_summary`, `metadata.rejected_sidecars`).** Every rejected payload lands in a sidecar
  row and in `rejected_summary` (each entry carries the row's `index` and the raw payload's title —
  `title_derived` when only the normaliser's positional id names it; an empty id or title is absent); the companion's
  rows are in its own `-companion.jsonl`, named on the envelope (`companion_voice.rejected_sidecar`, `null` and the file
  removed when nothing was rejected). `verdict-derive.sh` counts the rows of the sidecars the envelope names
  (`rejected_sidecars`): at start the run moves the previous run's envelope and its two sidecars aside (`.prev`) and it
  lists the sidecars it produced; a run that writes its envelope drops the `.prev` files; a run that aborts leaves NO envelope
  at the path and the `.prev` files beside it (the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback);
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG` scopes the NAMES — `adversarial-rejected-<gate>[-companion][-<tag>].jsonl` — so a chunk driver
  passes its chunk key and nothing is renamed afterwards (a tag outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` becomes a short hash of its
  raw value, said once, so distinct tags never share a file). A non-empty sidecar a listing envelope does not name is never
  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a
  chunk driver clears the directory's rejected set at the start of a round). Without an envelope, or without that field,
  every `adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl` beside the envelope's place counts. A pre-FR-2 envelope (no metadata at all,
  or a metadata without a `rejected_summary` key and without any FR-2 marker — `rejected_sidecars`, `companion_voice`;
  never `rejected_count`, which the writer before cycle-126 set too) counts none of the rows as old as itself, with a
  warning — historical sprints keep their verdicts — but a sidecar NEWER than it counts (one git tracks with its committed
  bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout gave it). Rows whose repair succeeded
  never count; a trailer-less file is held to the contract too; the same section with one top-level bullet per payload
  clears it in every case.
- **Wait cap and reaping (`failure_class: timeout`).** The second voice is reaped on INT/TERM/EXIT (one cleanup trap for
  the whole run, the whole process tree — re-collected after the freeze and before KILL — TERM then KILL after
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS`, the companion's pid trusted only while its start token matches the one recorded at
  the fork) and by a wait cap measured from its start: each `*-headless` hop counts the CLI adapter's bound — connect +
  max(600 s, the catalog's per-model `headless_timeout_seconds`, CLI hops only, capped at 3,600 s when the catalog loads;
  `claude-headless` carries 900 s because a dissent on `claude -p` takes 6–10 minutes; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT` is
  the fallback for a hop no catalog lists; a listed hop without the key is bound by the formula, 610 s) — each HTTP hop `timeout_seconds`, plus its lock wait and the CLI bound when its catalog chain falls through to a CLI
  hop (it takes that binary's lock before its request, as a `queue` phase; cheval walks the chain inside one call), plus
  30 s (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS` pins it). The deadline follows the companion's phase (queue → hop → post) under a global ceiling; the post-hop work
  (validation, repair round-trips) has its own budget, so a model that answered is never reaped mid-processing; the
  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on
  the shared hop the primary waits for the settled record). The previous run's envelope and sidecars are moved aside at
  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed
  (0 cents, `status: budget_exceeded`, exit 4).

  holder in flight for `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 5). A diff that prepares to no content is refused
  before the run lock (`status: nothing_to_review` under `--json`, exit 1, no call made); a top-priority file not even one
  hunk of which fits the budget is sent as its PARTIAL marker alone (`0 of N hunks shown`).
- **`failure_class` and `last_error`.** The class follows cheval's exit codes — 4 (`MISSING_API_KEY`) `auth`; 6
  (`BUDGET_EXCEEDED` / `RATE_LIMITED`) or a diagnostic saying "rate limit" / "429" / "quota" `quota`; 3 / 124 `timeout`,
  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
  receives the envelope and the sidecars.
- **Repairs (`repair_hops_skipped`, `repair_budget_exhausted`).** The repair round-trip walks `tiny` (with an Anthropic
  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)
  gives way to the description's 200-character head (counted in characters, never bytes).
- **Credentials and ledgers.** Presence resolves per alias with override precedence (env → `.env.local` → `.env`: the
  first place that assigns a variable decides it, an empty assignment disables that alias; a provider with several
  aliases — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` — is present when any alias resolves non-empty; the value is never
  expanded). Both cheval invocations append to `.run/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` under the writers'
  flock (issue #689), so the hash chain stays linear.

**Repair loop (D-2.4).** The repair chain is `tiny` (when an Anthropic credential is present) →
`claude-headless` (when the binary is on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last — one bounded
attempt per hop, so a host with neither still repairs through its own primary; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL`
pins the whole chain to one model (the round-1 hardening above has the retirement, lock and budget rules).
KF-004 evidence: the three real rejected payloads under `tests/fixtures/dissent-rejected/` now pass without a repair.

## Numeric anchors and the budget scaling (cycle-131 FR-4)

- **Numeric anchors (`anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`).** Both prompts ask each voice for the head-file line the finding
  sits on (`anchor_line`) and, for a range, its last line (`anchor_line_end`), beside the symbol `anchor` and
  `anchor_type`. The symbol anchor stays the stable reference and stays required for high-severity findings: the
  anchor check, `anchor_stability` and the hallucination filter key on `anchor` alone. The normaliser keeps a line only
  as a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, and an end only beside a kept start and at least it; any other value is
  dropped silently, never a rejection or a repair hop. A finding with no line is unchanged. Graders (the eval harness's
  envelope reduction) read `anchor_line` with the anchor's file as `path:line[-end]`; read them as a pointer, never as
  a replacement for the symbol.
- **Budget scaling (`budget_scale`, `budget_cents_max`).** `flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale`
  is `fixed` (the default; an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte) or `diff`: the budget becomes
  `min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)` (`budget_cents_max` default 600), where the estimate
  is the gate's own pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices. An estimate above that budget still refuses (exit 4,
  `status: budget_exceeded`, `reason: budget`). A malformed scale or maximum is said and `fixed` applies. When the key is
  written, the envelope's metadata carries `budget_scale`, `budget_cents_effective` and `budget_cents_max`. The eval
  harness writes `diff` for both gates in its sandbox config; the shipped default stays `fixed`.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# chart-unblock-probe.sh: the only way a `decision:unblock` ticket runs anything (SDD D-4.12).
     4	#
     5	# An unblock ticket answers a question that blocks a decision ("does the lib build on bash 3.2?",
     6	# "what does the API return?"). It may run read-only probes and throwaway worktrees; it never
     7	# writes App-Zone code in the main tree. This helper records the main tree's
     8	# `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` (every untracked file and
     9	# every ignored path that matches a pattern), runs the probe argv inside a detached worktree
    10	# under `mktemp -d` (cwd = that worktree), removes the worktree by an EXIT/INT/TERM trap on every
    11	# path, and exits 1 when the main tree's status changed. The probe's own exit code is printed
    12	# (`probe-exit: N`, 124 on a timeout) and is information for the ticket, not this helper's verdict.
    13	#
    14	# Usage: chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket <bead-id> [--timeout <s>] -- <cmd> [args...]
    15	# Exit: 0 main tree unchanged; 1 main tree changed (the ticket fails) or the worktree could not
    16	#       be created; 2 usage.
    17	# =============================================================================
    18	export LC_ALL=C
    19	set -euo pipefail
    20	
    21	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    22	# shellcheck source=/dev/null
    23	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/compat-lib.sh"
    24	
    25	TICKET=""
    26	TIMEOUT=600
    27	usage(){ echo "chart-unblock-probe: $*" >&2; echo "usage: chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket <bead-id> [--timeout <s>] -- <cmd> [args...]" >&2; exit 2; }
    28	
    29	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    30	  case "$1" in
    31	    --ticket) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--ticket needs a bead id"; TICKET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    32	    --timeout) [[ "${2:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,4}$ ]] || usage "--timeout needs seconds (1-99999)"; TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    33	    --) shift; break ;;
    34	    -h|--help) sed -n '2,16p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    35	    *) usage "unknown argument '$1' (the probe command goes after --)" ;;
    36	  esac
    37	done
    38	[[ -n "$TICKET" ]] || usage "--ticket is required"
    39	[[ "$TICKET" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$ ]] || usage "--ticket must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$"
    40	[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage "a probe command is required after --"
    41	
    42	MAIN="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "chart-unblock-probe: not inside a git work tree" >&2; exit 1; }
    43	SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/chart-probe.XXXXXX")"
    44	WT=""
    45	cleanup(){
    46	  if [[ -n "$WT" ]]; then
    47	    git -C "$MAIN" worktree remove --force "$WT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    48	    git -C "$MAIN" worktree prune >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    49	  fi
    50	  if [[ -n "$SCRATCH" && -d "$SCRATCH" ]]; then rm -rf -- "$SCRATCH"; fi
    51	  return 0
    52	}
    53	trap cleanup EXIT
    54	trap 'exit 130' INT
    55	trap 'exit 143' TERM
    56	
    57	before="$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching 2>/dev/null)"
    58	if ! git -C "$MAIN" worktree add --detach "${SCRATCH}/wt" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    59	  echo "chart-unblock-probe: could not create a throwaway worktree; nothing ran" >&2
    60	  exit 1
    61	fi
    62	WT="${SCRATCH}/wt"
    63	
    64	echo "chart-unblock-probe: ticket ${TICKET}: running in a throwaway worktree (timeout ${TIMEOUT}s)" >&2
    65	set +e
    66	(cd "$WT" && run_with_timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$@")
    67	rc=$?
    68	set -e
    69	echo "probe-exit: ${rc}"
    70	
    71	after="$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching 2>/dev/null)"
    72	if [[ "$before" != "$after" ]]; then
    73	  echo "chart-unblock-probe: FAIL: the probe changed the main tree; an unblock ticket never writes there. Changed entries:" >&2
    74	  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$before") <(printf '%s\n' "$after") | grep -E '^[<>]' | tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177' >&2 || true
    75	  exit 1
    76	fi
    77	exit 0

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# chart-guard.sh: the first step of every /chart invocation (charting-decisions skill).
     4	#
     5	# /chart is interactive only: a map whose destination and fog rounds the agent answered for
     6	# itself is not a map (PRD Appendix E D12, SDD D-4.3 step 0). This guard asks the decision
     7	# ledger writer for the context (`dec-write-lib.sh context`: a fresh unattended marker, a RUNNING
     8	# run state, LOA_UNATTENDED=1, LOA_FLATLINE_MODE=autonomous or an autonomous PRD Status line) and
     9	# refuses when it says `unattended`. It also refuses when `br` is missing, because a map lives on
    10	# beads.
    11	#
    12	# Usage:
    13	#   chart-guard.sh                    # chart or work a map
    14	#   chart-guard.sh --close-consumed   # `/chart close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle>`: the one
    15	#                                     # operation allowed unattended (SDD D-4.5)
    16	#   chart-guard.sh --root DIR         # fixture tree: its prd.md feeds the PRD Status signal
    17	# Exit: 0 go (prints `interactive`, or `unattended` with --close-consumed); 1 refused; 2 usage.
    18	# =============================================================================
    19	export LC_ALL=C
    20	set -euo pipefail
    21	
    22	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    23	ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd -P)"
    24	DW="${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
    25	CLOSE_CONSUMED=0
    26	
    27	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    28	  case "$1" in
    29	    --close-consumed) CLOSE_CONSUMED=1; shift ;;
    30	    --root) [[ -n "${2:-}" && -d "${2:-}" ]] || { echo "chart-guard: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$(cd "$2" && pwd -P)"; shift 2 ;;
    31	    -h|--help) sed -n '2,18p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    32	    *) echo "chart-guard: unknown argument '$1' (usage: chart-guard.sh [--close-consumed] [--root DIR])" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    33	  esac
    34	done
    35	
    36	if [[ ! -x "$DW" ]]; then
    37	  echo "chart-guard: refused: ${DW#"${ROOT}/"} is missing, so the context cannot be checked; /chart does not run without it." >&2
    38	  exit 1
    39	fi
    40	
    41	# Fail closed: a context that cannot be read counts as unattended.
    42	ctx="$("$DW" context --prd "${ROOT}/grimoires/loa/prd.md" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)" || ctx="unknown"
    43	case "$ctx" in
    44	  interactive) ;;
    45	  unattended)
    46	    if [[ $CLOSE_CONSUMED -eq 0 ]]; then
    47	      echo "/chart is interactive: a map whose rounds the agent answered is not a map. Run it with the operator present." >&2
    48	      echo "chart-guard: refused (context: unattended; see why with: .claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh context --why)" >&2
    49	      exit 1
    50	    fi ;;
    51	  *)
    52	    echo "chart-guard: refused: the context could not be read (dec-write-lib.sh context printed '${ctx}'); /chart treats that as unattended." >&2
    53	    exit 1 ;;
    54	esac
    55	
    56	if ! command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    57	  echo "chart-guard: refused: br (beads_rust) is not on PATH. A map is an epic of question beads; install br (.claude/scripts/beads/install-br.sh) or plan without a map with /plan." >&2
    58	  exit 1
    59	fi
    60	
    61	echo "$ctx"

    52	}
    53	trap cleanup EXIT
    54	trap 'exit 130' INT
    55	trap 'exit 143' TERM
    56	
    57	before="$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching 2>/dev/null)"
    58	if ! git -C "$MAIN" worktree add --detach "${SCRATCH}/wt" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    59	  echo "chart-unblock-probe: could not create a throwaway worktree; nothing ran" >&2
    60	  exit 1
    61	fi
    62	WT="${SCRATCH}/wt"
    63	
    64	echo "chart-unblock-probe: ticket ${TICKET}: running in a throwaway worktree (timeout ${TIMEOUT}s)" >&2
    65	set +e

    69	echo "probe-exit: ${rc}"
    70	
    71	after="$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching 2>/dev/null)"

    73	  echo "chart-unblock-probe: FAIL: the probe changed the main tree; an unblock ticket never writes there. Changed entries:" >&2
    74	  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$before") <(printf '%s\n' "$after") | grep -E '^[<>]' | tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177' >&2 || true

    76	fi
